purpose: Measure requested allocation traffic, peak live-byte increase and retained bytes across construction, cold/warm/replay native hull queries and cleanup, with exact output checks.
qualification_prerequisite: The unchanged finite-field candidate broad qualification must complete all eleven commands and its assessor must pass before this trial begins.
features: Reuse the already-frozen csgrs no-default-feature native libraries with matched transitive feature metadata. No Cargo rebuild occurs during this trial.
baseline_scope_reason: Only the original 24x12 native case is already certified by the admitted runtime. The other three retain their previously recorded failures; failed work is not used as a resource baseline for successful hulls.
cache_state: Fresh process per sample; clear grammar caches, construct the original sphere once, run three STRICT queries consecutively on the same retained input with all previous outputs alive, then validate/serialize all outputs, drop input/outputs and clear grammar caches. Shared process-global scalar constants may remain.
measurements: peak live requested bytes above phase entry
whole lifecycle retained requested bytes after grammar cleanup
oracle: Every full position-order/triangle-row/certainty transcript must equal the independently checked late candidate transcript, including every warm and replay output. The baseline 24x12 transcript must also match. No display conversions or reduced samples.
interpretation: All three observations and paired resource deltas are retained. Variation is reported, never filtered; no samples are added or pooled. Allocator-instrumented timing is diagnostic only and is not combined with the earlier uninstrumented process timing screen. These are requested heap-byte counts, not usable allocator sizes, stack usage or RSS.
guards: Original 35 pending files, baseline source map, each frozen candidate map, input artifacts, linked libraries and binaries must remain unchanged. The trial performs no admission or runtime edits.
open_after_this_trial: common/unsupported/nonzero scalar-query timing and allocation evidence
independent directed adversarial/representation campaign and instrumentation coverage
final resource documentation and admission decision
